coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED, after real effort: no CERN geodetic-survey or metrology publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the underground LHCb cavern was found (JINST detector paper blocked by bot-detection/size limit; LHCb Upgrade Framework TDR only checked for bibliographic metadata; home.cern and lhcb-outreach.web.cern.ch state only the depth and nearby village, not coordinates). The numeric lat/lon value is inherited from an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for "CERN Point 8" (kept as src:lep-point-8-osm-nominatim in this record's top-level sources for provenance, matching the pattern used at site:cern-point-1-atlas); that geocoder source is not cited on this coordinate field because A17 forbids a geocoder backing a detector-kind point. Per v0.2 A23, kind is 'campus' (not 'detector') since no rank<=7 source gives a surveyed hall position; confidence is 'uncertain' and this note documents the gap, which the validator accepts as a warning-level approximate placement (coordinate-kind-approximate) rather than an error. VERIFIER FIX (2026-09-17): removed a self-contradictory earlier sentence that asserted, in this same note, both that 'kind is kept as detector' and that 'kind is kept as campus'; the field's actual value has always been 'campus' and only that is now stated.

depth.quote: It is 21 metres long, 10 metres high and 13 metres wide, and sits 100 metres below ground near the town of Ferney-Voltaire, France.

name: LHC Point 8 (LHCb)
notes: This is a NEW record, distinct from site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi (owned by historic-cern), which documents the same physical point during the LEP/DELPHI era. The two coexist and are not duplicates: they describe the same cavern at different eras with independently sourced facts.
REVIEW REQUIRED: coordinate is a geocoder value (kind: campus, confidence: approximate); no rank<=7 detector-kind coordinate was found after real effort in this session. See coordinates.note.

summary.plain: The underground cavern at Point 8 of the LHC ring, near the French town of Ferney-Voltaire, where the LHCb detector sits about 100 metres below ground.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 8, Ferney-Voltaire (Ain, France); houses the LHCb forward-spectrometer detector approximately 100 m below the surface. Previously the site of the LEP-era DELPHI detector (see site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi).
